keyed: C: End the stored definition at summarize; apply top 20 by VisitCount desc when querying the view.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Keep the materialized definition as a supported aggregation. Sorting and selecting the displayed results belong in the consuming query.

keyed: B: Store sum(ErrorCount) and sum(RequestCount) by Service, then divide their selected totals at query time.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Retain numerators and denominators separately. Define zero-denominator behavior in the consumer rather than using an unweighted mean of stored rates.

keyed: c: The deployment fails because the rule can no longer be resolved
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: If the data source a rule depends on is removed or changed to a different type in the source stage, the rule becomes invalid. Fabric validates rules before deploying and blocks the deployment with an error.

keyed: A: Spark Job Definitions have documented source-control and deployment-pipeline support, like notebooks.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Job definitions follow the notebook's CI/CD story: source control plus deployment pipelines.

keyed: C: A OneLake shortcut to the external location
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Shortcuts create a reference to data in ADLS Gen2, Amazon S3, or another Fabric item, so it appears in your lakehouse without duplication or a refresh schedule. Copy activities and dataflows both move data, which adds cost, latency, and a second copy to keep consistent.

keyed: B: Share only that report with the auditor, with no build or reshare rights
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Item-level sharing grants access to a single item without a workspace role, so the auditor sees only that report. A is wrong because any workspace role, even Viewer, lets the user see every item in the workspace. C is wrong because Contributor can edit and delete content, and hiding items is not a security boundary. D is wrong because publish to web makes the report public to anyone with the link, which is unacceptable for finance data.

keyed: A: `TRY_CAST(OrderDateText AS date)` in the insert query
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: `TRY_CAST` returns NULL for any value it cannot convert instead of raising an error, so the load completes and bad dates become NULL. B is wrong because the first bad row still makes the whole statement fail, and the CATCH block only handles the error after the insert stops. C is wrong because converting to a string does not produce a `date` value at all. D is wrong because "N/A" is not NULL, so `ISNULL` leaves it in place, and a fake 1900 date hides missing data.

keyed: D: Check delimiter, quote/escape, and header settings against the file; repeat preview before loading.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: A destination schema cannot compensate for fields split incorrectly at the source. Diagnose the parsed preview before tuning transport or execution order.

keyed: C: 240, because the single sale matches three dimension rows.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Reason about join cardinality before aggregation. Unique version keys do not protect a query that joins on a different repeated column.

keyed: A: The new rows are visible without any action, but the model's schema must be updated before the new column appears.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Direct Lake distinguishes data changes (picked up directly from OneLake) from schema changes (which require the model to take an update before new columns or tables exist in it).

keyed: C: SQL RLS applies at the engine to authorized client queries and reduces dependence on individual report implementations.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Secure the data tier for SQL consumers rather than rely solely on visual filters.

keyed: A: A DirectQuery fallback may occur for the masked table, potentially increasing query latency.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Model storage mode and security enforcement are coupled: SQL DDM can prevent pure Direct Lake execution.

keyed: B: The analyst can find the endorsed model and request permission; data access remains gated.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Marking a semantic model discoverable changes catalog visibility to eligible users without granting Read or Build.

keyed: B: Nora only, assuming her ADO account has the needed Git rights.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Tenant eligibility and provider authorization are separate checks; the allowed Fabric user can use another properly authorized Git identity.

keyed: C: Capacity X workspaces can be blocked while Y remains allowed, subject to any further delegated workspace overrides.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Current tenant administration supports scoped delegation to capacity/workspace admins, so the effective gate is not always a single immutable tenant toggle.

keyed: B: The unsupported item may be absent in the feature workspace even though the source retains it.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Source support drives branch materialization; never assume unsupported live items are cloned. Check current support list because capabilities evolve.

keyed: A: Verify target role memberships and labels independently; assess label-copy conditions and any user consent requirement.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Permissions are not copied automatically; sensitivity labels have conditional propagation. Validate access and labeling as distinct checks.

keyed: B: In the connected execution-context Warehouse (WH_FINANCE).
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Completed query history is recorded for the Warehouse/endpoint context where the SQL was executed, not automatically for every referenced object.

keyed: D: Design and validate the actual cross-engine data-level security model and remove unnecessary broad workspace roles
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: least privilege must be enforced at the appropriate storage and engine access paths.

keyed: A: Measure the entire path and size the SLA from observed processing and downstream delays.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: The documented polling cadence tells you when detection may occur. A defensible SLA also includes transformation, capacity contention, publication, and consumption. This is an engineering inference, not a Microsoft latency guarantee.

keyed: C: Test representative samples and false negatives, restrict raw access, and review regional availability.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Keep the transformation as one control in a larger design. This recommendation is an inference from the feature purpose and preview limitations, not legal assurance or a claim of measured detection accuracy.

keyed: C: Validate supported behavior and dependencies at representative scale rather than extrapolating script time alone
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Fast metadata operations do not prove complete dependency compatibility.

keyed: B: Keep PDFs in Lakehouse Files, process with Spark, and load curated relational data into Warehouse; both use OneLake.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: Choose engines from the required operations. A shared storage foundation does not make every item a file store or every endpoint writable.

keyed: A: Grant Storage Blob Data Reader to the executing identity at the required source scope.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: The target SQL permissions have already been supplied. Diagnose the independent source data authorization instead of adding unrelated Warehouse grants.

keyed: B: Create the table clone within the source Warehouse, optionally in a different schema, using the AT timestamp syntax.
answerKeyContradictions.explanation: A supported same-workspace cross-database SELECT does not imply cross-Warehouse clone support. Check both placement and retention before cloning.
